candidate.answerReason: The 12 nondancers formed two thirds of those remaining. Thus 18 people remained, and because that was half the original group, the original group contained 36 people, agreeing with C.

methods.label: Work backward with equal groups
methods.explanation:
Work backward from the \(12\) people who were not dancing. One third of those remaining danced, so the nondancers made up two of three equal groups.

Those two groups contained \(12\) people, so each group contained \(12\div2=6\) people. All three groups together therefore contained
\[
3\times6=18\text{ people}.
\]
These \(18\) people were the half who stayed. Doubling gives the original number:
\[
2\times18=36.
\]
The room originally contained \(36\) people, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Equal groups give an elementary way to recover the whole from two thirds, followed by doubling. No algebra is needed.
